t: This is West House, at 35 Glebe Place in Chelsea. It's a Queen Anne revival house, listed Grade Two star, and Historic England calls it one of the earliest examples of that style. Philip Webb designed it for the artist George Price Boyce, and it was built in 1868 and 1869. Webb is sometimes called the Father of Arts and Crafts Architecture, and he co-founded the Society for the Protection of Ancient Buildings. Inside, the house has one of the few triple-height ceilings in London.
